name: Prone Neck Bridge
description: The prone neck bridge is a gymnastics and wrestling exercise where the body is supported on the forehead or top of the head with the body arched and feet on the floor, loading the anterior cervical musculature with a significant portion of bodyweight. It develops exceptional cervical and spinal stability through an isometric hold against the entire bodyweight. Used extensively in wrestling, judo, and gymnastics conditioning, it represents the highest intensity isometric load a neck curl progression leads toward.

execution.starting_position: Lie face-down on a mat. Place the top of the forehead on the mat. Feet on the floor behind. Push up with the hands to begin, then lower to a supported position on the forehead only.
execution.setup_instructions: This is an ADVANCED exercise. Prerequisites: several months of neck curl and neck extension training, comfort with isometric neck loading. Begin with hand assistance.
steps: Step 1: Begin in a push-up-like position, forehead on the mat.
Step 2: Slowly walk the feet toward the head, increasing the load through the neck.
Step 3: Use the hands to control how much weight is transferred to the forehead.
Step 4: Hold the bridge position isometrically for the target duration.
Step 5: Use the hands to assist the return to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Attempting this without progressive neck training over months
Attempting the full bodyweight hold without hand-assisted progressions
Hyperextending the lower back, which is secondary to the neck position
safety_considerations: Contraindicated with any cervical pathology, disc issues, or acute pain
Must be preceded by weeks-to-months of progressive neck training
Always use hand-assisted variations before full bodyweight
Have a spotter when attempting for the first time
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Isometric hold — no movement through range. The goal is to maintain the bridge position.
coaching_cues: Hands assist as needed — don't be a hero
